# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1320
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1320
- **Title**: fix(1319): drop notifications landing on a disposed AgentService (openSession background history count)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1319-dispose-race` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +168
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T14:45:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T14:54:03Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1319

## Root cause

`FlutterSessionManager.openSession` → `AgentService.loadSession` ends with `unawaited(_refreshHistoryAbove())` (agent_service_sessions.dart:318). That fire-and-forget continuation suspends on real file I/O (`windowed.countAbove()` → `countRecords()` → ranged read), so it routinely resumes AFTER the caller has moved on — in the app after session-switch teardown, in the failing shard after test teardown. `AgentService.dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the refresh's existing generation guard (`gen != _loadGeneration`) passes, `_historyAboveCount` (null since the open) differs from the fresh count, and `_notify()` hits `ChangeNotifier.debugAssertNotDisposed` — the exact `failed after test completion` crash of run 37474096974 (job 112305916597, main be413ff5d5). Pure teardown-vs-continuation race, timing-dependent; not content-related to #1309's merge, as the issue suspected.

## Fix

Dispose-aware guard at the **shared notification chokepoint**: `AgentService._notify()` (agent_service.dart, the bridge every part-file extension must use because `notifyListeners` is `@protected`) now returns early when the existing `_disposed` flag is set — the same mechanism this codebase already uses per-site (`agent_service_runs.dart:80` guards the identical race on task settlements; same pattern in agent_service_inbox.dart, agent_service_sessions.dart:432).

Why the chokepoint rather than a guard inside `_refreshHistoryAbove` (one of the issue's options): every fire-and-forget continuation notifies through `_notify()`, so one guard covers this bug plus every current and future sibling (`_jumpToRecord`'s finally-notify, mid-loadSession disposal, run settlements) — a notification after dispose has no possible receiver, so dropping it is strictly correct. Diff: **8 insertions, 2 deletions, one hunk**; no test un-guarded, no behavior change for live services.

## Regression test (failing-first, deterministic)

New `flutter_app/test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` reuses the windowed suite's `GatedFileSystem` (the issue #1159 mid-flight freeze fixture) to park the background count's first ranged read, then disposes the service under it — the exact CI crash ordering, without timing dependence:

- **Unpatched (verified before the fix):** RED with the exact CI stack — `notifyListeners (change_notifier.dart:414) → AgentService._notify (agent_service.dart:2374) → _refreshHistoryAbove (agent_service_history.dart:108→101) → loadSession (agent_service_sessions.dart:318→225) → openSession (flutter_session_manager.dart:500→497)`.
- **Patched:** green.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The Mac lane host's system dart/flutter toolchain is unreliable (EPERM engine-stamp writes / VM SIGKILL exit 137), so the gates ran on a temp Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 SDK copy with a fleet pub-cache — same workaround as prior lanes:

- `flutter test test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart test/session_oversized_windowed_test.dart`: **8/8 pass** (includes the originally-red `UT-oversized-windowed`).
- Stability repeats: `UT-oversized-windowed` **10/10**, dispose-race test **10/10**.
- `flutter analyze` on both changed files: only a pre-existing unrelated info (`use_null_aware_elements` at agent_service.dart:1846, present on origin/main, untouched by this diff).
- `dart format`: both touched files clean; the rest of agent_service.dart was deliberately NOT reformatted (it is not format-clean on main; reformatting would pollute the diff).

CI is the real gate per fleet policy — no workflows were dispatched or rerunned from this lane.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: root-cause fix, deterministic failing-first regression test, both targeted suites green + repeat-verified. Remaining (owner/SM): merge-train CI run, the issue's 20× CI repeat confirmation — locally 10× green here; the fix also leaves `AgentService.dispose()` itself non-idempotent (double-dispose throws on `fsRevision.dispose()`), which no current caller does and is out of this issue's scope, noted for the review checklist.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1320
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1320
- **Title**: fix(1319): drop notifications landing on a disposed AgentService (openSession background history count)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1319-dispose-race` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +168
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T14:45:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T14:54:03Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1319

## Root cause

`FlutterSessionManager.openSession` → `AgentService.loadSession` ends with `unawaited(_refreshHistoryAbove())` (agent_service_sessions.dart:318). That fire-and-forget continuation suspends on real file I/O (`windowed.countAbove()` → `countRecords()` → ranged read), so it routinely resumes AFTER the caller has moved on — in the app after session-switch teardown, in the failing shard after test teardown. `AgentService.dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the refresh's existing generation guard (`gen != _loadGeneration`) passes, `_historyAboveCount` (null since the open) differs from the fresh count, and `_notify()` hits `ChangeNotifier.debugAssertNotDisposed` — the exact `failed after test completion` crash of run 37474096974 (job 112305916597, main be413ff5d5). Pure teardown-vs-continuation race, timing-dependent; not content-related to #1309's merge, as the issue suspected.

## Fix

Dispose-aware guard at the **shared notification chokepoint**: `AgentService._notify()` (agent_service.dart, the bridge every part-file extension must use because `notifyListeners` is `@protected`) now returns early when the existing `_disposed` flag is set — the same mechanism this codebase already uses per-site (`agent_service_runs.dart:80` guards the identical race on task settlements; same pattern in agent_service_inbox.dart, agent_service_sessions.dart:432).

Why the chokepoint rather than a guard inside `_refreshHistoryAbove` (one of the issue's options): every fire-and-forget continuation notifies through `_notify()`, so one guard covers this bug plus every current and future sibling (`_jumpToRecord`'s finally-notify, mid-loadSession disposal, run settlements) — a notification after dispose has no possible receiver, so dropping it is strictly correct. Diff: **8 insertions, 2 deletions, one hunk**; no test un-guarded, no behavior change for live services.

## Regression test (failing-first, deterministic)

New `flutter_app/test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` reuses the windowed suite's `GatedFileSystem` (the issue #1159 mid-flight freeze fixture) to park the background count's first ranged read, then disposes the service under it — the exact CI crash ordering, without timing dependence:

- **Unpatched (verified before the fix):** RED with the exact CI stack — `notifyListeners (change_notifier.dart:414) → AgentService._notify (agent_service.dart:2374) → _refreshHistoryAbove (agent_service_history.dart:108→101) → loadSession (agent_service_sessions.dart:318→225) → openSession (flutter_session_manager.dart:500→497)`.
- **Patched:** green.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The Mac lane host's system dart/flutter toolchain is unreliable (EPERM engine-stamp writes / VM SIGKILL exit 137), so the gates ran on a temp Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 SDK copy with a fleet pub-cache — same workaround as prior lanes:

- `flutter test test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart test/session_oversized_windowed_test.dart`: **8/8 pass** (includes the originally-red `UT-oversized-windowed`).
- Stability repeats: `UT-oversized-windowed` **10/10**, dispose-race test **10/10**.
- `flutter analyze` on both changed files: only a pre-existing unrelated info (`use_null_aware_elements` at agent_service.dart:1846, present on origin/main, untouched by this diff).
- `dart format`: both touched files clean; the rest of agent_service.dart was deliberately NOT reformatted (it is not format-clean on main; reformatting would pollute the diff).

CI is the real gate per fleet policy — no workflows were dispatched or rerunned from this lane.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: root-cause fix, deterministic failing-first regression test, both targeted suites green + repeat-verified. Remaining (owner/SM): merge-train CI run, the issue's 20× CI repeat confirmation — locally 10× green here; the fix also leaves `AgentService.dispose()` itself non-idempotent (double-dispose throws on `fsRevision.dispose()`), which no current caller does and is out of this issue's scope, noted for the review checklist.

## Root cause

`FlutterSessionManager.openSession` → `AgentService.loadSession` ends with `unawaited(_refreshHistoryAbove())` (agent_service_sessions.dart:318). That fire-and-forget continuation suspends on real file I/O (`windowed.countAbove()` → `countRecords()` → ranged read), so it routinely resumes AFTER the caller has moved on — in the app after session-switch teardown, in the failing shard after test teardown. `AgentService.dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the refresh's existing generation guard (`gen != _loadGeneration`) passes, `_historyAboveCount` (null since the open) differs from the fresh count, and `_notify()` hits `ChangeNotifier.debugAssertNotDisposed` — the exact `failed after test completion` crash of run 37474096974 (job 112305916597, main be413ff5d5). Pure teardown-vs-continuation race, timing-dependent; not content-related to #1309's merge, as the issue suspected.

## Fix

Dispose-aware guard at the **shared notification chokepoint**: `AgentService._notify()` (agent_service.dart, the bridge every part-file extension must use because `notifyListeners` is `@protected`) now returns early when the existing `_disposed` flag is set — the same mechanism this codebase already uses per-site (`agent_service_runs.dart:80` guards the identical race on task settlements; same pattern in agent_service_inbox.dart, agent_service_sessions.dart:432).

Why the chokepoint rather than a guard inside `_refreshHistoryAbove` (one of the issue's options): every fire-and-forget continuation notifies through `_notify()`, so one guard covers this bug plus every current and future sibling (`_jumpToRecord`'s finally-notify, mid-loadSession disposal, run settlements) — a notification after dispose has no possible receiver, so dropping it is strictly correct. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1320
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1320
- **Title**: fix(1319): drop notifications landing on a disposed AgentService (openSession background history count)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1319-dispose-race` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +168
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T14:45:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T14:54:03Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1319

## Root cause

`FlutterSessionManager.openSession` → `AgentService.loadSession` ends with `unawaited(_refreshHistoryAbove())` (agent_service_sessions.dart:318). That fire-and-forget continuation suspends on real file I/O (`windowed.countAbove()` → `countRecords()` → ranged read), so it routinely resumes AFTER the caller has moved on — in the app after session-switch teardown, in the failing shard after test teardown. `AgentService.dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the refresh's existing generation guard (`gen != _loadGeneration`) passes, `_historyAboveCount` (null since the open) differs from the fresh count, and `_notify()` hits `ChangeNotifier.debugAssertNotDisposed` — the exact `failed after test completion` crash of run 37474096974 (job 112305916597, main be413ff5d5). Pure teardown-vs-continuation race, timing-dependent; not content-related to #1309's merge, as the issue suspected.

## Fix

Dispose-aware guard at the **shared notification chokepoint**: `AgentService._notify()` (agent_service.dart, the bridge every part-file extension must use because `notifyListeners` is `@protected`) now returns early when the existing `_disposed` flag is set — the same mechanism this codebase already uses per-site (`agent_service_runs.dart:80` guards the identical race on task settlements; same pattern in agent_service_inbox.dart, agent_service_sessions.dart:432).

Why the chokepoint rather than a guard inside `_refreshHistoryAbove` (one of the issue's options): every fire-and-forget continuation notifies through `_notify()`, so one guard covers this bug plus every current and future sibling (`_jumpToRecord`'s finally-notify, mid-loadSession disposal, run settlements) — a notification after dispose has no possible receiver, so dropping it is strictly correct. Diff: **8 insertions, 2 deletions, one hunk**; no test un-guarded, no behavior change for live services.

## Regression test (failing-first, deterministic)

New `flutter_app/test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` reuses the windowed suite's `GatedFileSystem` (the issue #1159 mid-flight freeze fixture) to park the background count's first ranged read, then disposes the service under it — the exact CI crash ordering, without timing dependence:

- **Unpatched (verified before the fix):** RED with the exact CI stack — `notifyListeners (change_notifier.dart:414) → AgentService._notify (agent_service.dart:2374) → _refreshHistoryAbove (agent_service_history.dart:108→101) → loadSession (agent_service_sessions.dart:318→225) → openSession (flutter_session_manager.dart:500→497)`.
- **Patched:** green.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The Mac lane host's system dart/flutter toolchain is unreliable (EPERM engine-stamp writes / VM SIGKILL exit 137), so the gates ran on a temp Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 SDK copy with a fleet pub-cache — same workaround as prior lanes:

- `flutter test test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart test/session_oversized_windowed_test.dart`: **8/8 pass** (includes the originally-red `UT-oversized-windowed`).
- Stability repeats: `UT-oversized-windowed` **10/10**, dispose-race test **10/10**.
- `flutter analyze` on both changed files: only a pre-existing unrelated info (`use_null_aware_elements` at agent_service.dart:1846, present on origin/main, untouched by this diff).
- `dart format`: both touched files clean; the rest of agent_service.dart was deliberately NOT reformatted (it is not format-clean on main; reformatting would pollute the diff).

CI is the real gate per fleet policy — no workflows were dispatched or rerunned from this lane.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: root-cause fix, deterministic failing-first regression test, both targeted suites green + repeat-verified. Remaining (owner/SM): merge-train CI run, the issue's 20× CI repeat confirmation — locally 10× green here; the fix also leaves `AgentService.dispose()` itself non-idempotent (double-dispose throws on `fsRevision.dispose()`), which no current caller does and is out of this issue's scope, noted for the review checklist.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1320
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1320
- **Title**: fix(1319): drop notifications landing on a disposed AgentService (openSession background history count)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1319-dispose-race` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +168
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T14:45:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T14:54:03Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1319

## Root cause

`FlutterSessionManager.openSession` → `AgentService.loadSession` ends with `unawaited(_refreshHistoryAbove())` (agent_service_sessions.dart:318). That fire-and-forget continuation suspends on real file I/O (`windowed.countAbove()` → `countRecords()` → ranged read), so it routinely resumes AFTER the caller has moved on — in the app after session-switch teardown, in the failing shard after test teardown. `AgentService.dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the refresh's existing generation guard (`gen != _loadGeneration`) passes, `_historyAboveCount` (null since the open) differs from the fresh count, and `_notify()` hits `ChangeNotifier.debugAssertNotDisposed` — the exact `failed after test completion` crash of run 37474096974 (job 112305916597, main be413ff5d5). Pure teardown-vs-continuation race, timing-dependent; not content-related to #1309's merge, as the issue suspected.

## Fix

Dispose-aware guard at the **shared notification chokepoint**: `AgentService._notify()` (agent_service.dart, the bridge every part-file extension must use because `notifyListeners` is `@protected`) now returns early when the existing `_disposed` flag is set — the same mechanism this codebase already uses per-site (`agent_service_runs.dart:80` guards the identical race on task settlements; same pattern in agent_service_inbox.dart, agent_service_sessions.dart:432).

Why the chokepoint rather than a guard inside `_refreshHistoryAbove` (one of the issue's options): every fire-and-forget continuation notifies through `_notify()`, so one guard covers this bug plus every current and future sibling (`_jumpToRecord`'s finally-notify, mid-loadSession disposal, run settlements) — a notification after dispose has no possible receiver, so dropping it is strictly correct. Diff: **8 insertions, 2 deletions, one hunk**; no test un-guarded, no behavior change for live services.

## Regression test (failing-first, deterministic)

New `flutter_app/test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` reuses the windowed suite's `GatedFileSystem` (the issue #1159 mid-flight freeze fixture) to park the background count's first ranged read, then disposes the service under it — the exact CI crash ordering, without timing dependence:

- **Unpatched (verified before the fix):** RED with the exact CI stack — `notifyListeners (change_notifier.dart:414) → AgentService._notify (agent_service.dart:2374) → _refreshHistoryAbove (agent_service_history.dart:108→101) → loadSession (agent_service_sessions.dart:318→225) → openSession (flutter_session_manager.dart:500→497)`.
- **Patched:** green.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The Mac lane host's system dart/flutter toolchain is unreliable (EPERM engine-stamp writes / VM SIGKILL exit 137), so the gates ran on a temp Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 SDK copy with a fleet pub-cache — same workaround as prior lanes:

- `flutter test test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart test/session_oversized_windowed_test.dart`: **8/8 pass** (includes the originally-red `UT-oversized-windowed`).
- Stability repeats: `UT-oversized-windowed` **10/10**, dispose-race test **10/10**.
- `flutter analyze` on both changed files: only a pre-existing unrelated info (`use_null_aware_elements` at agent_service.dart:1846, present on origin/main, untouched by this diff).
- `dart format`: both touched files clean; the rest of agent_service.dart was deliberately NOT reformatted (it is not format-clean on main; reformatting would pollute the diff).

CI is the real gate per fleet policy — no workflows were dispatched or rerunned from this lane.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: root-cause fix, deterministic failing-first regression test, both targeted suites green + repeat-verified. Remaining (owner/SM): merge-train CI run, the issue's 20× CI repeat confirmation — locally 10× green here; the fix also leaves `AgentService.dispose()` itself non-idempotent (double-dispose throws on `fsRevision.dispose()`), which no current caller does and is out of this issue's scope, noted for the review checklist.

- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1319-dispose-race` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +168
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T14:45:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T14:54:03Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1319

## Root cause

`FlutterSessionManager.openSession` → `AgentService.loadSession` ends with `unawaited(_refreshHistoryAbove())` (agent_service_sessions.dart:318). That fire-and-forget continuation suspends on real file I/O (`windowed.countAbove()` → `countRecords()` → ranged read), so it routinely resumes AFTER the caller has moved on — in the app after session-switch teardown, in the failing shard after test teardown. `AgentService.dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the refresh's existing generation guard (`gen != _loadGeneration`) passes, `_historyAboveCount` (null since the open) differs from the fresh count, and `_notify()` hits `ChangeNotifier.debugAssertNotDisposed` — the exact `failed after test completion` crash of run 37474096974 (job 112305916597, main be413ff5d5). Pure teardown-vs-continuation race, timing-dependent; not content-related to #1309's merge, as the issue suspected.

## Fix

Dispose-aware guard at the **shared notification chokepoint**: `AgentService._notify()` (agent_service.dart, the bridge every part-file extension must use because `notifyListeners` is `@protected`) now returns early when the existing `_disposed` flag is set — the same mechanism this codebase already uses per-site (`agent_service_runs.dart:80` guards the identical race on task settlements; same pattern in agent_service_inbox.dart, agent_service_sessions.dart:432).

Why the chokepoint rather than a guard inside `_refreshHistoryAbove` (one of the issue's options): every fire-and-forget continuation notifies through `_notify()`, so one guard covers this bug plus every current and future sibling (`_jumpToRecord`'s finally-notify, mid-loadSession disposal, run settlements) — a notification after dispose has no possible receiver, so dropping it is strictly correct. Diff: **8 insertions, 2 deletions, one hunk**; no test un-guarded, no behavior change for live services.

## Regression test (failing-first, deterministic)

New `flutter_app/test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` reuses the windowed suite's `GatedFileSystem` (the issue #1159 mid-flight freeze fixture) to park the background count's first ranged read, then disposes the service under it — the exact CI crash ordering, without timing dependence:

- **Unpatched (verified before the fix):** RED with the exact CI stack — `notifyListeners (change_notifier.dart:414) → AgentService._notify (agent_service.dart:2374) → _refreshHistoryAbove (agent_service_history.dart:108→101) → loadSession (agent_service_sessions.dart:318→225) → openSession (flutter_session_manager.dart:500→497)`.
- **Patched:** green.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The Mac lane host's system dart/flutter toolchain is unreliable (EPERM engine-stamp writes / VM SIGKILL exit 137), so the gates ran on a temp Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 SDK copy with a fleet pub-cache — same workaround as prior lanes:

- `flutter test test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart test/session_oversized_windowed_test.dart`: **8/8 pass** (includes the originally-red `UT-oversized-windowed`).
- Stability repeats: `UT-oversized-windowed` **10/10**, dispose-race test **10/10**.
- `flutter analyze` on both changed files: only a pre-existing unrelated info (`use_null_aware_elements` at agent_service.dart:1846, present on origin/main, untouched by this diff).
- `dart format`: both touched files clean; the rest of agent_service.dart was deliberately NOT reformatted (it is not format-clean on main; reformatting would pollute the diff).

CI is the real gate per fleet policy — no workflows were dispatched or rerunned from this lane.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: root-cause fix, deterministic failing-first regression test, both targeted suites green + repeat-verified. Remaining (owner/SM): merge-train CI run, the issue's 20× CI repeat confirmation — locally 10× green here; the fix also leaves `AgentService.dispose()` itself non-idempotent (double-dispose throws on `fsRevision.dispose()`), which no current caller does and is out of this issue's scope, noted for the review checklist.

2. However, there's a subtle race: `_notify` checks `_disposed`, but a continuation could resume between the check and `notifyListeners()` — no, Dart is single-threaded (event loop), so no true data race; once `_disposed` is true it stays true. So the guard is sound for the crash.

Actually in release mode, `_debugAssertNotDisposed` is compiled out, and notifyListeners would call listeners — after dispose, `_listeners` is cleared... - **Title**: fix(1319): drop notifications landing on a disposed AgentService (openSession background history count)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1319-dispose-race` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +168
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T14:45:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T14:54:03Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1319

## Root cause

`FlutterSessionManager.openSession` → `AgentService.loadSession` ends with `unawaited(_refreshHistoryAbove())` (agent_service_sessions.dart:318). That fire-and-forget continuation suspends on real file I/O (`windowed.countAbove()` → `countRecords()` → ranged read), so it routinely resumes AFTER the caller has moved on — in the app after session-switch teardown, in the failing shard after test teardown. `AgentService.dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the refresh's existing generation guard (`gen != _loadGeneration`) passes, `_historyAboveCount` (null since the open) differs from the fresh count, and `_notify()` hits `ChangeNotifier.debugAssertNotDisposed` — the exact `failed after test completion` crash of run 37474096974 (job 112305916597, main be413ff5d5). # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1320
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1320
- **Title**: fix(1319): drop notifications landing on a disposed AgentService (openSession background history count)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1319-dispose-race` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +168
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T14:45:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T14:54:03Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1319

## Root cause

`FlutterSessionManager.openSession` → `AgentService.loadSession` ends with `unawaited(_refreshHistoryAbove())` (agent_service_sessions.dart:318). That fire-and-forget continuation suspends on real file I/O (`windowed.countAbove()` → `countRecords()` → ranged read), so it routinely resumes AFTER the caller has moved on — in the app after session-switch teardown, in the failing shard after test teardown. `AgentService.dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the refresh's existing generation guard (`gen != _loadGeneration`) passes, `_historyAboveCount` (null since the open) differs from the fresh count, and `_notify()` hits `ChangeNotifier.debugAssertNotDisposed` — the exact `failed after test completion` crash of run 37474096974 (job 112305916597, main be413ff5d5). Pure teardown-vs-continuation race, timing-dependent; not content-related to #1309's merge, as the issue suspected.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1320
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1320
- **Title**: fix(1319): drop notifications landing on a disposed AgentService (openSession background history count)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1319-dispose-race` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +168
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T14:45:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T14:54:03Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1319

## Root cause

`FlutterSessionManager.openSession` → `AgentService.loadSession` ends with `unawaited(_refreshHistoryAbove())` (agent_service_sessions.dart:318). That fire-and-forget continuation suspends on real file I/O (`windowed.countAbove()` → `countRecords()` → ranged read), so it routinely resumes AFTER the caller has moved on — in the app after session-switch teardown, in the failing shard after test teardown. `AgentService.dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the refresh's existing generation guard (`gen != _loadGeneration`) passes, `_historyAboveCount` (null since the open) differs from the fresh count, and `_notify()` hits `ChangeNotifier.debugAssertNotDisposed` — the exact `failed after test completion` crash of run 37474096974 (job 112305916597, main be413ff5d5). Pure teardown-vs-continuation race, timing-dependent; not content-related to #1309's merge, as the issue suspected.

## Fix

Dispose-aware guard at the **shared notification chokepoint**: `AgentService._notify()` (agent_service.dart, the bridge every part-file extension must use because `notifyListeners` is `@protected`) now returns early when the existing `_disposed` flag is set — the same mechanism this codebase already uses per-site (`agent_service_runs.dart:80` guards the identical race on task settlements; same pattern in agent_service_inbox.dart, agent_service_sessions.dart:432).

Why the chokepoint rather than a guard inside `_refreshHistoryAbove` (one of the issue's options): every fire-and-forget continuation notifies through `_notify()`, so one guard covers this bug plus every current and future sibling (`_jumpToRecord`'s finally-notify, mid-loadSession disposal, run settlements) — a notification after dispose has no possible receiver, so dropping it is strictly correct. Diff: **8 insertions, 2 deletions, one hunk**; no test un-guarded, no behavior change for live services.

## Regression test (failing-first, deterministic)

New `flutter_app/test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` reuses the windowed suite's `GatedFileSystem` (the issue #1159 mid-flight freeze fixture) to park the background count's first ranged read, then disposes the service under it — the exact CI crash ordering, without timing dependence:

- **Unpatched (verified before the fix):** RED with the exact CI stack — `notifyListeners (change_notifier.dart:414) → AgentService._notify (agent_service.dart:2374) → _refreshHistoryAbove (agent_service_history.dart:108→101) → loadSession (agent_service_sessions.dart:318→225) → openSession (flutter_session_manager.dart:500→497)`.
- **Patched:** green.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The Mac lane host's system dart/flutter toolchain is unreliable (EPERM engine-stamp writes / VM SIGKILL exit 137), so the gates ran on a temp Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 SDK copy with a fleet pub-cache — same workaround as prior lanes:

- `flutter test test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart test/session_oversized_windowed_test.dart`: **8/8 pass** (includes the originally-red `UT-oversized-windowed`).
- Stability repeats: `UT-oversized-windowed` **10/10**, dispose-race test **10/10**.
- `flutter analyze` on both changed files: only a pre-existing unrelated info (`use_null_aware_elements` at agent_service.dart:1846, present on origin/main, untouched by this diff).
- `dart format`: both touched files clean; the rest of agent_service.dart was deliberately NOT reformatted (it is not format-clean on main; reformatting would pollute the diff).

CI is the real gate per fleet policy — no workflows were dispatched or rerunned from this lane.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: root-cause fix, deterministic failing-first regression test, both targeted suites green + repeat-verified. Remaining (owner/SM): merge-train CI run, the issue's 20× CI repeat confirmation — locally 10× green here; the fix also leaves `AgentService.dispose()` itself non-idempotent (double-dispose throws on `fsRevision.dispose()`), which no current caller does and is out of this issue's scope, noted for the review checklist.

- **State**: open

- **Additions**: +168
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T14:45:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T14:54:03Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1319

## Root cause

`FlutterSessionManager.openSession` → `AgentService.loadSession` ends with `unawaited(_refreshHistoryAbove())` (agent_service_sessions.dart:318). That fire-and-forget continuation suspends on real file I/O (`windowed.countAbove()` → `countRecords()` → ranged read), so it routinely resumes AFTER the caller has moved on — in the app after session-switch teardown, in the failing shard after test teardown. `AgentService.dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the refresh's existing generation guard (`gen != _loadGeneration`) passes, `_historyAboveCount` (null since the open) differs from the fresh count, and `_notify()` hits `ChangeNotifier.debugAssertNotDisposed` — the exact `failed after test completion` crash of run 37474096974 (job 112305916597, main be413ff5d5). Pure teardown-vs-continuation race, timing-dependent; not content-related to #1309's merge, as the issue suspected.

## Fix

Dispose-aware guard at the **shared notification chokepoint**: `AgentService._notify()` (agent_service.dart, the bridge every part-file extension must use because `notifyListeners` is `@protected`) now returns early when the existing `_disposed` flag is set — the same mechanism this codebase already uses per-site (`agent_service_runs.dart:80` guards the identical race on task settlements; same pattern in agent_service_inbox.dart, agent_service_sessions.dart:432).

Why the chokepoint rather than a guard inside `_refreshHistoryAbove` (one of the issue's options): every fire-and-forget continuation notifies through `_notify()`, so one guard covers this bug plus every current and future sibling (`_jumpToRecord`'s finally-notify, mid-loadSession disposal, run settlements) — a notification after dispose has no possible receiver, so dropping it is strictly correct. Diff: **8 insertions, 2 deletions, one hunk**; no test un-guarded, no behavior change for live services.

## Regression test (failing-first, deterministic)

New `flutter_app/test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` reuses the windowed suite's `GatedFileSystem` (the issue #1159 mid-flight freeze fixture) to park the background count's first ranged read, then disposes the service under it — the exact CI crash ordering, without timing dependence:

- **Unpatched (verified before the fix):** RED with the exact CI stack — `notifyListeners (change_notifier.dart:414) → AgentService._notify (agent_service.dart:2374) → _refreshHistoryAbove (agent_service_history.dart:108→101) → loadSession (agent_service_sessions.dart:318→225) → openSession (flutter_session_manager.dart:500→497)`.
- **Patched:** green.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The Mac lane host's system dart/flutter toolchain is unreliable (EPERM engine-stamp writes / VM SIGKILL exit 137), so the gates ran on a temp Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 SDK copy with a fleet pub-cache — same workaround as prior lanes:

- `flutter test test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart test/session_oversized_windowed_test.dart`: **8/8 pass** (includes the originally-red `UT-oversized-windowed`).
- Stability repeats: `UT-oversized-windowed` **10/10**, dispose-race test **10/10**.
- `flutter analyze` on both changed files: only a pre-existing unrelated info (`use_null_aware_elements` at agent_service.dart:1846, present on origin/main, untouched by this diff).
- `dart format`: both touched files clean; the rest of agent_service.dart was deliberately NOT reformatted (it is not format-clean on main; reformatting would pollute the diff).

CI is the real gate per fleet policy — no workflows were dispatched or rerunned from this lane.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: root-cause fix, deterministic failing-first regression test, both targeted suites green + repeat-verified. Remaining (owner/SM): merge-train CI run, the issue's 20× CI repeat confirmation — locally 10× green here; the fix also leaves `AgentService.dispose()` itself non-idempotent (double-dispose throws on `fsRevision.dispose()`), which no current caller does and is out of this issue's scope, noted for the review checklist.

2. However, there's a subtle race: `_notify` checks `_disposed`, but a continuation could resume between the check and `notifyListeners()` — no, Dart is single-threaded (event loop), so no true data race; once `_disposed` is true it stays true. So the guard is sound for the crash.

4. Also `debugAssertNotDisposed` — in the test, the assertion fired in debug mode. Actually in release mode, `_debugAssertNotDisposed` is compiled out, and notifyListeners would call listeners — after dispose, `_listeners` is cleared... Actually dispose() in ChangeNotifier sets _listeners to null in newer Flutter? Let me recall: ChangeNotifier.dispose() sets `_count = 0`, `_listeners = new List...` — it doesn't null out.    - Timing: `armGate()` then 20ms delay, dispose, releaseGate, 20ms delay. The 20ms delays are timing heuristics but the gate makes ordering deterministic-ish. Is there a possibility the continuation already passed the gated read before armGate? The comment says "By the time openSession resolves, the only remaining reader is the unawaited history count — suspended inside its stat, about to hit the first gated ranged read." Hmm — is that guaranteed? If the count completes before armGate on a slow machine, the test would pass trivially without testing anything (false positive). But the gate is armed right after openSession resolves; the count suspends at the first gated ranged read. If the machine is slow and the count finishes first... then the test passes without exercising the race → flaky-as-in-never-fails test. But the PR says verified failing-first (RED unpatched), so at least in their environment it exercises it. 20ms windows: could be flaky on heavily loaded CI. But acceptable for a regression test? # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1320
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1320
- **Title**: fix(1319): drop notifications landing on a disposed AgentService (openSession background history count)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1319-dispose-race` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +168
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T14:45:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T14:54:03Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1319

## Root cause

`FlutterSessionManager.openSession` → `AgentService.loadSession` ends with `unawaited(_refreshHistoryAbove())` (agent_service_sessions.dart:318). That fire-and-forget continuation suspends on real file I/O (`windowed.countAbove()` → `countRecords()` → ranged read), so it routinely resumes AFTER the caller has moved on — in the app after session-switch teardown, in the failing shard after test teardown. `AgentService.dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the refresh's existing generation guard (`gen != _loadGeneration`) passes, `_historyAboveCount` (null since the open) differs from the fresh count, and `_notify()` hits `ChangeNotifier.debugAssertNotDisposed` — the exact `failed after test completion` crash of run 37474096974 (job 112305916597, main be413ff5d5). Pure teardown-vs-continuation race, timing-dependent; not content-related to #1309's merge, as the issue suspected.

## Fix

Dispose-aware guard at the **shared notification chokepoint**: `AgentService._notify()` (agent_service.dart, the bridge every part-file extension must use because `notifyListeners` is `@protected`) now returns early when the existing `_disposed` flag is set — the same mechanism this codebase already uses per-site (`agent_service_runs.dart:80` guards the identical race on task settlements; same pattern in agent_service_inbox.dart, agent_service_sessions.dart:432).

Why the chokepoint rather than a guard inside `_refreshHistoryAbove` (one of the issue's options): every fire-and-forget continuation notifies through `_notify()`, so one guard covers this bug plus every current and future sibling (`_jumpToRecord`'s finally-notify, mid-loadSession disposal, run settlements) — a notification after dispose has no possible receiver, so dropping it is strictly correct. Diff: **8 insertions, 2 deletions, one hunk**; no test un-guarded, no behavior change for live services.

## Regression test (failing-first, deterministic)

New `flutter_app/test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` reuses the windowed suite's `GatedFileSystem` (the issue #1159 mid-flight freeze fixture) to park the background count's first ranged read, then disposes the service under it — the exact CI crash ordering, without timing dependence:

- **Unpatched (verified before the fix):** RED with the exact CI stack — `notifyListeners (change_notifier.dart:414) → AgentService._notify (agent_service.dart:2374) → _refreshHistoryAbove (agent_service_history.dart:108→101) → loadSession (agent_service_sessions.dart:318→225) → openSession (flutter_session_manager.dart:500→497)`.
- **Patched:** green.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The Mac lane host's system dart/flutter toolchain is unreliable (EPERM engine-stamp writes / VM SIGKILL exit 137), so the gates ran on a temp Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 SDK copy with a fleet pub-cache — same workaround as prior lanes:

- `flutter test test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart test/session_oversized_windowed_test.dart`: **8/8 pass** (includes the originally-red `UT-oversized-windowed`).
- Stability repeats: `UT-oversized-windowed` **10/10**, dispose-race test **10/10**.
- `flutter analyze` on both changed files: only a pre-existing unrelated info (`use_null_aware_elements` at agent_service.dart:1846, present on origin/main, untouched by this diff).
- `dart format`: both touched files clean; the rest of agent_service.dart was deliberately NOT reformatted (it is not format-clean on main; reformatting would pollute the diff).

CI is the real gate per fleet policy — no workflows were dispatched or rerunned from this lane.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: root-cause fix, deterministic failing-first regression test, both targeted suites green + repeat-verified. Remaining (owner/SM): merge-train CI run, the issue's 20× CI repeat confirmation — locally 10× green here; the fix also leaves `AgentService.dispose()` itself non-idempotent (double-dispose throws on `fsRevision.dispose()`), which no current caller does and is out of this issue's scope, noted for the review checklist.

- **Title**: fix(1319): drop notifications landing on a disposed AgentService (openSession background history count)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1319-dispose-race` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +168
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T14:45:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T14:54:03Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1319

## Root cause

`FlutterSessionManager.openSession` → `AgentService.loadSession` ends with `unawaited(_refreshHistoryAbove())` (agent_service_sessions.dart:318). That fire-and-forget continuation suspends on real file I/O (`windowed.countAbove()` → `countRecords()` → ranged read), so it routinely resumes AFTER the caller has moved on — in the app after session-switch teardown, in the failing shard after test teardown. `AgentService.dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the refresh's existing generation guard (`gen != _loadGeneration`) passes, `_historyAboveCount` (null since the open) differs from the fresh count, and `_notify()` hits `ChangeNotifier.debugAssertNotDisposed` — the exact `failed after test completion` crash of run 37474096974 (job 112305916597, main be413ff5d5). Pure teardown-vs-continuation race, timing-dependent; not content-related to #1309's merge, as the issue suspected.

## Fix

Dispose-aware guard at the **shared notification chokepoint**: `AgentService._notify()` (agent_service.dart, the bridge every part-file extension must use because `notifyListeners` is `@protected`) now returns early when the existing `_disposed` flag is set — the same mechanism this codebase already uses per-site (`agent_service_runs.dart:80` guards the identical race on task settlements; same pattern in agent_service_inbox.dart, agent_service_sessions.dart:432).

Why the chokepoint rather than a guard inside `_refreshHistoryAbove` (one of the issue's options): every fire-and-forget continuation notifies through `_notify()`, so one guard covers this bug plus every current and future sibling (`_jumpToRecord`'s finally-notify, mid-loadSession disposal, run settlements) — a notification after dispose has no possible receiver, so dropping it is strictly correct. Diff: **8 insertions, 2 deletions, one hunk**; no test un-guarded, no behavior change for live services.

## Regression test (failing-first, deterministic)

New `flutter_app/test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` reuses the windowed suite's `GatedFileSystem` (the issue #1159 mid-flight freeze fixture) to park the background count's first ranged read, then disposes the service under it — the exact CI crash ordering, without timing dependence:

- **Unpatched (verified before the fix):** RED with the exact CI stack — `notifyListeners (change_notifier.dart:414) → AgentService._notify (agent_service.dart:2374) → _refreshHistoryAbove (agent_service_history.dart:108→101) → loadSession (agent_service_sessions.dart:318→225) → openSession (flutter_session_manager.dart:500→497)`.
- **Patched:** green.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The Mac lane host's system dart/flutter toolchain is unreliable (EPERM engine-stamp writes / VM SIGKILL exit 137), so the gates ran on a temp Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 SDK copy with a fleet pub-cache — same workaround as prior lanes:

- `flutter test test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart test/session_oversized_windowed_test.dart`: **8/8 pass** (includes the originally-red `UT-oversized-windowed`).
- Stability repeats: `UT-oversized-windowed` **10/10**, dispose-race test **10/10**.
- `flutter analyze` on both changed files: only a pre-existing unrelated info (`use_null_aware_elements` at agent_service.dart:1846, present on origin/main, untouched by this diff).
- `dart format`: both touched files clean; the rest of agent_service.dart was deliberately NOT reformatted (it is not format-clean on main; reformatting would pollute the diff).

CI is the real gate per fleet policy — no workflows were dispatched or rerunned from this lane.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: root-cause fix, deterministic failing-first regression test, both targeted suites green + repeat-verified. Remaining (owner/SM): merge-train CI run, the issue's 20× CI repeat confirmation — locally 10× green here; the fix also leaves `AgentService.dispose()` itself non-idempotent (double-dispose throws on `fsRevision.dispose()`), which no current caller does and is out of this issue's scope, noted for the review checklist.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. - **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit

- **State**: open

- **Additions**: +168
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T14:45:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T14:54:03Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1319

## Root cause

`FlutterSessionManager.openSession` → `AgentService.loadSession` ends with `unawaited(_refreshHistoryAbove())` (agent_service_sessions.dart:318). That fire-and-forget continuation suspends on real file I/O (`windowed.countAbove()` → `countRecords()` → ranged read), so it routinely resumes AFTER the caller has moved on — in the app after session-switch teardown, in the failing shard after test teardown. `AgentService.dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the refresh's existing generation guard (`gen != _loadGeneration`) passes, `_historyAboveCount` (null since the open) differs from the fresh count, and `_notify()` hits `ChangeNotifier.debugAssertNotDisposed` — the exact `failed after test completion` crash of run 37474096974 (job 112305916597, main be413ff5d5). Pure teardown-vs-continuation race, timing-dependent; not content-related to #1309's merge, as the issue suspected.

## Fix

Dispose-aware guard at the **shared notification chokepoint**: `AgentService._notify()` (agent_service.dart, the bridge every part-file extension must use because `notifyListeners` is `@protected`) now returns early when the existing `_disposed` flag is set — the same mechanism this codebase already uses per-site (`agent_service_runs.dart:80` guards the identical race on task settlements; same pattern in agent_service_inbox.dart, agent_service_sessions.dart:432).

Why the chokepoint rather than a guard inside `_refreshHistoryAbove` (one of the issue's options): every fire-and-forget continuation notifies through `_notify()`, so one guard covers this bug plus every current and future sibling (`_jumpToRecord`'s finally-notify, mid-loadSession disposal, run settlements) — a notification after dispose has no possible receiver, so dropping it is strictly correct. Diff: **8 insertions, 2 deletions, one hunk**; no test un-guarded, no behavior change for live services.

## Regression test (failing-first, deterministic)

New `flutter_app/test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` reuses the windowed suite's `GatedFileSystem` (the issue #1159 mid-flight freeze fixture) to park the background count's first ranged read, then disposes the service under it — the exact CI crash ordering, without timing dependence:

- **Unpatched (verified before the fix):** RED with the exact CI stack — `notifyListeners (change_notifier.dart:414) → AgentService._notify (agent_service.dart:2374) → _refreshHistoryAbove (agent_service_history.dart:108→101) → loadSession (agent_service_sessions.dart:318→225) → openSession (flutter_session_manager.dart:500→497)`.
- **Patched:** green.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The Mac lane host's system dart/flutter toolchain is unreliable (EPERM engine-stamp writes / VM SIGKILL exit 137), so the gates ran on a temp Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 SDK copy with a fleet pub-cache — same workaround as prior lanes:

- `flutter test test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart test/session_oversized_windowed_test.dart`: **8/8 pass** (includes the originally-red `UT-oversized-windowed`).
- Stability repeats: `UT-oversized-windowed` **10/10**, dispose-race test **10/10**.
- `flutter analyze` on both changed files: only a pre-existing unrelated info (`use_null_aware_elements` at agent_service.dart:1846, present on origin/main, untouched by this diff).
- `dart format`: both touched files clean; the rest of agent_service.dart was deliberately NOT reformatted (it is not format-clean on main; reformatting would pollute the diff).

CI is the real gate per fleet policy — no workflows were dispatched or rerunned from this lane.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: root-cause fix, deterministic failing-first regression test, both targeted suites green + repeat-verified. Remaining (owner/SM): merge-train CI run, the issue's 20× CI repeat confirmation — locally 10× green here; the fix also leaves `AgentService.dispose()` itself non-idempotent (double-dispose throws on `fsRevision.dispose()`), which no current caller does and is out of this issue's scope, noted for the review checklist.

- **State**: open

- **Additions**: +168
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T14:45:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T14:54:03Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1319

## Root cause

`FlutterSessionManager.openSession` → `AgentService.loadSession` ends with `unawaited(_refreshHistoryAbove())` (agent_service_sessions.dart:318). That fire-and-forget continuation suspends on real file I/O (`windowed.countAbove()` → `countRecords()` → ranged read), so it routinely resumes AFTER the caller has moved on — in the app after session-switch teardown, in the failing shard after test teardown. `AgentService.dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the refresh's existing generation guard (`gen != _loadGeneration`) passes, `_historyAboveCount` (null since the open) differs from the fresh count, and `_notify()` hits `ChangeNotifier.debugAssertNotDisposed` — the exact `failed after test completion` crash of run 37474096974 (job 112305916597, main be413ff5d5). Pure teardown-vs-continuation race, timing-dependent; not content-related to #1309's merge, as the issue suspected.

## Fix

Dispose-aware guard at the **shared notification chokepoint**: `AgentService._notify()` (agent_service.dart, the bridge every part-file extension must use because `notifyListeners` is `@protected`) now returns early when the existing `_disposed` flag is set — the same mechanism this codebase already uses per-site (`agent_service_runs.dart:80` guards the identical race on task settlements; same pattern in agent_service_inbox.dart, agent_service_sessions.dart:432).

Why the chokepoint rather than a guard inside `_refreshHistoryAbove` (one of the issue's options): every fire-and-forget continuation notifies through `_notify()`, so one guard covers this bug plus every current and future sibling (`_jumpToRecord`'s finally-notify, mid-loadSession disposal, run settlements) — a notification after dispose has no possible receiver, so dropping it is strictly correct. Diff: **8 insertions, 2 deletions, one hunk**; no test un-guarded, no behavior change for live services.

## Regression test (failing-first, deterministic)

New `flutter_app/test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` reuses the windowed suite's `GatedFileSystem` (the issue #1159 mid-flight freeze fixture) to park the background count's first ranged read, then disposes the service under it — the exact CI crash ordering, without timing dependence:

- **Unpatched (verified before the fix):** RED with the exact CI stack — `notifyListeners (change_notifier.dart:414) → AgentService._notify (agent_service.dart:2374) → _refreshHistoryAbove (agent_service_history.dart:108→101) → loadSession (agent_service_sessions.dart:318→225) → openSession (flutter_session_manager.dart:500→497)`.
- **Patched:** green.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The Mac lane host's system dart/flutter toolchain is unreliable (EPERM engine-stamp writes / VM SIGKILL exit 137), so the gates ran on a temp Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 SDK copy with a fleet pub-cache — same workaround as prior lanes:

- `flutter test test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart test/session_oversized_windowed_test.dart`: **8/8 pass** (includes the originally-red `UT-oversized-windowed`).
- Stability repeats: `UT-oversized-windowed` **10/10**, dispose-race test **10/10**.
- `flutter analyze` on both changed files: only a pre-existing unrelated info (`use_null_aware_elements` at agent_service.dart:1846, present on origin/main, untouched by this diff).
- `dart format`: both touched files clean; the rest of agent_service.dart was deliberately NOT reformatted (it is not format-clean on main; reformatting would pollute the diff).

CI is the real gate per fleet policy — no workflows were dispatched or rerunned from this lane.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: root-cause fix, deterministic failing-first regression test, both targeted suites green + repeat-verified. Remaining (owner/SM): merge-train CI run, the issue's 20× CI repeat confirmation — locally 10× green here; the fix also leaves `AgentService.dispose()` itself non-idempotent (double-dispose throws on `fsRevision.dispose()`), which no current caller does and is out of this issue's scope, noted for the review checklist.

# dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: app-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. ## PR Description

Fixes #1319

## Root cause

`FlutterSessionManager.openSession` → `AgentService.loadSession` ends with `unawaited(_refreshHistoryAbove())` (agent_service_sessions.dart:318). That fire-and-forget continuation suspends on real file I/O (`windowed.countAbove()` → `countRecords()` → ranged read), so it routinely resumes AFTER the caller has moved on — in the app after session-switch teardown, in the failing shard after test teardown. `AgentService.dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the refresh's existing generation guard (`gen != _loadGeneration`) passes, `_historyAboveCount` (null since the open) differs from the fresh count, and `_notify()` hits `ChangeNotifier.debugAssertNotDisposed` — the exact `failed after test completion` crash of run 37474096974 (job 112305916597, main be413ff5d5). Pure teardown-vs-continuation race, timing-dependent; not content-related to #1309's merge, as the issue suspected.

## Fix

Dispose-aware guard at the **shared notification chokepoint**: `AgentService._notify()` (agent_service.dart, the bridge every part-file extension must use because `notifyListeners` is `@protected`) now returns early when the existing `_disposed` flag is set — the same mechanism this codebase already uses per-site (`agent_service_runs.dart:80` guards the identical race on task settlements; same pattern in agent_service_inbox.dart, agent_service_sessions.dart:432).

Why the chokepoint rather than a guard inside `_refreshHistoryAbove` (one of the issue's options): every fire-and-forget continuation notifies through `_notify()`, so one guard covers this bug plus every current and future sibling (`_jumpToRecord`'s finally-notify, mid-loadSession disposal, run settlements) — a notification after dispose has no possible receiver, so dropping it is strictly correct. Diff: **8 insertions, 2 deletions, one hunk**; no test un-guarded, no behavior change for live services.

## Regression test (failing-first, deterministic)

New `flutter_app/test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` reuses the windowed suite's `GatedFileSystem` (the issue #1159 mid-flight freeze fixture) to park the background count's first ranged read, then disposes the service under it — the exact CI crash ordering, without timing dependence:

- **Unpatched (verified before the fix):** RED with the exact CI stack — `notifyListeners (change_notifier.dart:414) → AgentService._notify (agent_service.dart:2374) → _refreshHistoryAbove (agent_service_history.dart:108→101) → loadSession (agent_service_sessions.dart:318→225) → openSession (flutter_session_manager.dart:500→497)`.
- **Patched:** green.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The Mac lane host's system dart/flutter toolchain is unreliable (EPERM engine-stamp writes / VM SIGKILL exit 137), so the gates ran on a temp Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 SDK copy with a fleet pub-cache — same workaround as prior lanes:

- `dart format`: both touched files clean; the rest of agent_service.dart was deliberately NOT reformatted (it is not format-clean on main; reformatting would pollute the diff).

# dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: app-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1320
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1320
- **Title**: fix(1319): drop notifications landing on a disposed AgentService (openSession background history count)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1319-dispose-race` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +168
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T14:45:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T14:54:03Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1319

## Root cause

`FlutterSessionManager.openSession` → `AgentService.loadSession` ends with `unawaited(_refreshHistoryAbove())` (agent_service_sessions.dart:318). That fire-and-forget continuation suspends on real file I/O (`windowed.countAbove()` → `countRecords()` → ranged read), so it routinely resumes AFTER the caller has moved on — in the app after session-switch teardown, in the failing shard after test teardown. `AgentService.dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the refresh's existing generation guard (`gen != _loadGeneration`) passes, `_historyAboveCount` (null since the open) differs from the fresh count, and `_notify()` hits `ChangeNotifier.debugAssertNotDisposed` — the exact `failed after test completion` crash of run 37474096974 (job 112305916597, main be413ff5d5). # dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: app-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3.
